content.comment_body: I have established a connection between my PC and [product_name] [version_no], loaded the program, and everything seems fine. My [product_name] uses IP 192.168.0.33, while my PC is at 192.168.1.58. When I download the program, it enables 192.168.0.254 and the device runs. In the connection center, I see the PC IP as 192.168.1.58. I'm unsure if this setup is correct. If I try accessing 192.168.0.33 via a browser, there is no connection to [product_name]. Can someone point out what I'm missing? I can't write in English well. Possibly, the issue is with [product_name] Ethernet tools, as I can't move past the displayed settings. [IMAGE] [IMAGE]
Why did you post here instead of your own topic? Do you think this will get you a quicker response?
If I knew how to do it, I would. I get criticism about my writing but not much help.

[product_name] (IP 192.168.0.33) and the PC (IP 192.168.1.58) are not on the same subnet. You need to assign an IP so both are within the same subnet, such as: [product_name] (IP 192.168.0.33) and PC (IP 192.168.0.58), or [product_name] (IP 192.168.1.33) and PC (IP 192.168.1.58).

You aren't being criticized for your content, but for not posting in English. You're asking questions in Italian and expect others to translate them. It's better if you translate your questions into English so everyone can assist you more easily.

PC and [product_name] are linked: 192.168.0.254 is the PC's IP, and 192.168.0.33 is [product_name]'s IP. Communication works fine. However, when I use a browser and go to https://192.168.0.33, it doesn't connect to [product_name]; I need this to control the device and see its display via browser controls.
You won't get help with such a statement.

PC and [product_name] are linked: 192.168.0.254 is the PC's IP, and 192.168.0.33 is [product_name]'s IP. Communication is OK. However, using the browser to reach https://192.168.0.33 does not connect, and I need this for viewing and controlling [product_name] with arrows.
Hello. How do you change the IP of [product_name] [version_no]? Currently, it's 192.168.0.33, but I want to set it to 192.168.1.58.
You shouldn't assign the same IP address to [product_name] and your PC. They must be in the same subnet but have different unique IP addresses.
An IP address consists of four parts: XXX.YYY.ZZZ.nnn. The first three specify the subnet, and the last part identifies the device.
Check the attached PDF.

My issue is that [product_name] is at 192.168.0.33 and my PC is at 192.168.1.58. When I load the program using [product_name] software, it asks to change the PC's IP; after accepting, it becomes 192.168.0.254, and everything works. Now, for remote control, when I enter http://192.168.0.33:8080 in the browser, the [product_name] image should appear, but it doesn't work despite many attempts. This led me to want to move [product_name]'s IP to 192.168.1.nn to match my server's network and try accessing it via http://192.168.1.nn. Was I clear? How do you restore [product_name] [version_no] to factory settings?

Because your PC is in a different subnet, [product_name] software creates a temporary IP for your PC to communicate with [product_name]. Once you quit the software or shut down the PC, the temporary IP disappears. To change [product_name]'s IP, create a small program (for example, I1 on Q1). Set the desired IP (192.168.1.33), with subnet mask 255.255.255.0, in the file properties, then transfer this to [product_name] using the temporary IP (192.168.0.254). During the transfer, the software will ask if the IP should be overwritten; confirm to change [product_name]'s IP to 192.168.1.33. For remote access, simply entering the port after the IP (like 192.168.1.33:8080) may not work if your router blocks the connection. Activate port forwarding on your router for port 8080 to 8080, but be cautious, as this exposes your device to security risks. Using DynDNS or VPN is safer for remote control.

Hello, Check Youtube for a video demonstrating how to change IP settings. [url]

You misunderstood. You should create a program with the new IP address (192.168.1.33), then transfer it to [product_name] which currently has IP 192.168.0.33. Only after transfer and overwriting does [product_name] hold the new IP.

Most likely, the issue now is due to the current password set on [product_name]. Both myself and others have attempted to change the password, but errors occurred. Does anyone know how to re-enter the initial starter program?

If you changed the password and are stuck in operator mode without knowing the password, you’re in a tough spot. Factory reset isn’t available from the [product_name] menu in operator mode; you’ll need to use the application software to perform a factory reset.
How can I reload the initial program? Is there a video or location to download it?
There isn’t a dedicated initial program. Open the application software, then go to Tools > Transfer > Factory Reset.

It’s important to understand that both your PC and [product_name] must be in the same subnet; that means their first three IP numbers should match. There are advanced ways to work across different subnets, but those are complex for beginners. An easy way to test access: open the application software and search for controllers; once it creates a temporary IP (x.y.z.254), start your browser and input your [product_name]'s IP address. The software should run in the background during this. If you want to use the web server independently, put both devices in the same subnet. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user is having difficulty connecting to a [product_name] device’s web interface, despite being able to transfer and run programs. The root cause is network misconfiguration—specifically, mismatched PC and device subnets. Although the PC and [product_name] communicate at a basic level, web-based control does not function, prompting multiple questions about IP settings, password recovery, and factory resets.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants straightforward instructions on configuring network settings so they can connect to the [product_name] device’s web server from their PC browser for remote monitoring and control. Clarity regarding IP assignment, subnetting, and web access would help resolve their connectivity issues.
